name: SPX3819M5-L-3-3_TR
title: 500 mA low-noise LDO voltage regulator
summary: The SPX3819 is a positive low-dropout linear regulator for loads up to 500 mA, with 340 mV typical dropout at full load and 90 µA typical ground current at light load. It comes with fixed outputs from 1.2 V to 5.0 V, or adjustable from 1.235 V, in SOT-23-5, NSOIC-8 and 2 × 3 mm DFN-8. A logic enable switches it off to near-zero current, and on fixed versions a BYP pin lets a capacitor quiet the reference, bringing output noise down to 40 µVRMS. Current limit, thermal shutdown and reverse-battery protection are built in. SPX3819M5-L-3-3/TR is the 3.3 V SOT-23-5 version.
key_figures: 2.5 V to 16 V operating; -20 V to +20 V absolute
340 mV typ, 550 mV max at 500 mA

circuits.title: Standard application circuit
circuits.description: A fixed-output SPX3819 in SOT-23-5 fed from a battery. A polarised capacitor from VOUT to ground keeps the loop stable. EN is brought out as a control line and may instead be joined to VIN. The capacitor on BYP is optional: with it the output is quieter and start-up slower; without it the part turns on fastest.

parts.note: output capacitor, polarised; 1 µF tantalum or 2.2 µF aluminium electrolytic
optional; 10 nF on BYP lowers output noise

notes: EN may be tied directly to VIN.

circuits.title: Typical adjustable output voltage configuration
circuits.description: The adjustable SPX3819 in SOT-23-5 fed from a battery. R1 from VOUT to ADJ and R2 from ADJ to ground set the output to 1.235 V × (1 + R1/R2). A polarised capacitor holds the output. EN is a control line: high runs the regulator, low turns it off.

parts.note: ADJ to ground; above 10 kΩ, 22 kΩ to 47 kΩ for best results

equations.name: Adjustable output voltage
equations.note: R2 is to be more than 10 kΩ; 22 kΩ to 47 kΩ gives the best results.

where.θJA: junction-to-ambient thermal resistance of the package

operation.text: The regulator limits its output current, shuts down when the die overheats, and survives a reversed battery. Its power dissipation is limited internally.
With EN low the regulator is off and draws almost nothing: quiescent current is 0.05 µA typical at VENABLE ≤ 0.4 V. EN above 2.0 V turns it on; below 0.4 V turns it off.

Stability needs an output capacitor whose size depends on the circuit and grows with load current: a 10 mA load needs about half the capacitance of a 150 mA load. A good 2.2 µF aluminium electrolytic is stable in most circuits, and a 1 µF tantalum often is too. Electrolytics vary widely at high frequency by type and maker, so the type and value are settled by bench test.
On the adjustable part the smallest stable output capacitance falls as the output voltage is set higher, because the loop gain rises.

On fixed versions BYP gives access to the internal reference. 10 nF from BYP to ground cuts the output noise substantially; where noise does not matter BYP may be left open. Start-up time grows with the BYP capacitor, so a larger capacitor gives a slower rise of the output, and leaving it off gives the fastest turn-on.

Output noise is 300 µVRMS typical from 10 Hz to 100 kHz without a bypass capacitor and as low as 40 µVRMS with one. The low temperature coefficient of the output also lets the part serve as a low-power voltage reference.
